column2: WASTE CONTRACTOR EVALUATION — Know Who Is Disposing of Your Waste
Your business is legally responsible for your waste until it reaches a licensed facility. Use this scorecard to evaluate your current contractor and decide if you need to make changes.

column3: Verify at your local DONRE office or online portal

column2: Waste Types They Are Licensed to Handle
EVALUATION CRITERIA — Score 1 to 5 for each criterion

Licence & Legal Compliance
Holds current, valid waste collection licence issued by DONRE. Licence covers the waste types you generate.
column6: Request licence certificate. Verify number at DONRE website or office.

column2:
Disposal Documentation
Provides waste transfer notes, disposal manifests, or receipts for every collection.
column6: Ask for sample documentation from last 3 collections.

column2:
Hazardous Waste Handling
Certified to handle hazardous waste (if applicable). Provides hazardous waste manifests.
column6: Request specific hazardous waste licence if you produce hazardous waste.

column2:
Actual Disposal Practice
You have verified (or have reasonable confidence) that waste is taken to a licensed facility — not illegally dumped.
column6: Request facility address and check it is registered. Ask to visit if possible.

column2:
Reliability & Service Quality
Collections happen on agreed schedule. Responsive to issues. Clear contact person.
column6: Review your own experience over past 6 months.

column2:
Separation Integrity
Contractor actually keeps separated waste streams separate — does not mix them in the vehicle.
column6: Observe a collection or ask staff who are present at collections.

column2:
Pricing Transparency
Pricing is clear, documented, and reflects actual volumes. No unexplained charges.
column6: Review last 6 months of invoices against agreed rates.

column2: IF CONTRACTOR SCORES < 2.5 — ALTERNATIVE CONTRACTOR CHECKLIST
Use this checklist when evaluating alternative contractors. Do NOT sign any contract before verifying all CRITICAL items.

column3: Holds current DONRE waste collection licence covering your waste types
Provides waste transfer notes or manifests for every collection
Can provide the address of the licensed disposal facility they use
Has a minimum 2 years operating history — ask for references
Willing to sign a written service agreement with disposal documentation obligations
Collection frequency matches your operational needs
Pricing is documented and includes all fees (no hidden charges)
Has a dedicated contact person for service issues
